questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Matrices of Quadratic Forms
questions.problem:
Which of the following could be matrices of quadratic forms defined on ${R}^{3}?$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & -3 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -3 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ -2 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that every quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ has an associated $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

With that in mind, let's examine each matrix in turn.

- $T$ could be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it is a $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

- $U$ could also be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it is a $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

- $V$ *cannot* be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it's a $2\times 2$ matrix (not $3\times 3$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "$T$ and $U$ only."

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Given the matrix $A$ above, evaluate the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Substituting $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ into the expression for $Q(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}^{T}\,Ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the quadratic form 
$Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2}.$ 
Evaluate $Q(x)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting this into the expression for $Q(x)$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2}-3\cdot 1\cdot (-4)-0\cdot (-4)+(-4)^{2} \\  & =1+12+0+16 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Quadratic Form Given Its Matrix
questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{x}_{j}$ in the expression of the quadratic form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =2{x}_{1}{x}_{1}+(-4){x}_{1}{x}_{2}+(-4){x}_{2}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{x}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-4{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a quadratic form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2} \\ -4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-4{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{x}_{j}$ in the expression of the quadratic form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =2{x}_{1}{x}_{1}+(3){x}_{1}{x}_{2}+(3){x}_{2}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{x}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a quadratic form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & b \\ b & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ is given above. What is the value of $b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the matrix of the quadratic form must be symmetric, we rewrite our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+1{x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\  & +\,1{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+(-2){x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that to get a symmetric matrix, we must split the coefficient of $2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ between the entries 

$$
{a}_{12}={a}_{21}=\frac{2}{2}=1
$$

of our matrix. So, the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $b=1$ and $c=-2.$ Finally, 

$$
b+c=1-2=-1.
$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & b \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ b & 0 & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+3{x}_{3}^{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the matrix of the quadratic form must be symmetric, we rewrite our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+1{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+(-5){x}_{1}{x}_{3} \\  & +\,1{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}^{2}+0{x}_{2}{x}_{3} \\  & +\,(-5){x}_{3}{x}_{1}+0{x}_{3}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that to get a symmetric matrix, we must do the following splits:

- we split the coefficient of $2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ between the entries ${a}_{12}={a}_{21}=\frac{2}{2}=1,$ and

- we split the coefficient of $-10{x}_{1}{x}_{3}$ between the entries ${a}_{13}={a}_{31}=\frac{-10}{2}=-5.$

So, the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=3,$ $b=-5,$ and $c=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=3+(-5)+3=1.
$$

\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})+{x}_{2}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}) \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
